review.summary: Accept with corrections. Scope is clean: only allowed paths changed, protected blobs identical, git status empty; PREDECLARED (a6c66e9b) and amendment A1 (2681f19a) precede every declared-size run; policy C unchanged. My own script rebuilt every deciding number from the raw logs: 0 mismatches with RESULTS.json; regenerated RESULTS.json and REPORT_KO.md are identical. Re-runs: 30 declared runs reproduce all counters, audits and state bits (instructions within 2e-6); 6 timing cells meeting the rule give B speed-ups within 3% of the reported ones; my own references agree below 1e-10. Tests, sentinels, clippy, fmt pass on HEAD. Verdicts: validity PASS, cadence PASS 4/4, policy PASS 4/4 (pre-declared geometric mean), KILL not triggered. Corrections: KILL label NOT_RUN is wrong; policy attempts exceed 1.10 at the worst grid point on 2 families (1.44, 1.23); 149/149/33 cusp1d solves hit the Krylov budget and lie outside the checks; the gain is confounded with restart length (protected driver at restart 10 costs 0.26-0.37 of restart 40; B/A at equal restart 0.64-0.78, exploratory); three binaries, not two; load ranges; unlisted report-script edit.

findings.correction: Record KILL as evaluated and not triggered, not as NOT_RUN.

findings.claim: Builder report: policy PASS (C) with attempts <= 1.10 on 4 of 4 families, stated without qualification.
findings.evidence: The family statistic declared before the runs (PREDECLARED.json matched_error_rule.family_statistic, commit a6c66e9b) is the geometric mean over a 201-point grid: 1.009, 1.005, 1.000, 1.003. Equal-tolerance maxima: 1.017, 0.999, 1.000, 1.023. The worst grid point is 1.439 on cusp1d (E about 7.0e-7: C needs 1225 attempts at rtol 1e-7, A reached 6.7e-7 with 853 attempts at rtol 1e-6) and 1.226 on bruss1d (E 3.76e-5: A 44 attempts at rtol 1e-3, C interpolated 54 because its error at 1e-3 is 27% larger). With the worst grid point as statistic only 2 of 4 families meet 1.10. REPORT_KO.md section 3.3 says this; the summary does not.
findings.correction: Keep PASS (statistic fixed before the runs) and record next to it that the attempts part holds for the geometric mean and at equal tolerance, and exceeds 1.10 at the worst grid point on cusp1d (1.44) and bruss1d (1.23).

findings.claim: Builder report: zero failed residual checks; the residual check passes in every solve.
findings.evidence: logs/runs/cusp1d__*__audit1.log: linear_solve_failures of arm A 55, 46, 34, 11, 3 (149), arm B the same 149 (client failed_solves), arm C 9, 15, 6, 2, 1 (33). These solves ended with 'GMRES exhausted 200 Arnoldi vectors'; the attempt was rejected and retried with a smaller step. They are outside the checks by the pre-declared definition (PREDECLARED.json residual_check: checks = solves the arm completed). A and B have the same count, so B is not worse than the protected driver. REPORT_KO.md sections 1 and 3.1 do not state these counts.
findings.correction: State the validity result as 'among completed solves' and add the counts of budget-exhausted solves for cusp1d (A 149, B 149, C 33).

findings.claim: The summary attributes the gain of arm B to the residual-test cadence without qualification.
findings.evidence: Builder's exploratory logs (logs/exploratory, rtol 1e-5 only, achieved error identical in three families and within 3% on cusp1d), recomputed by me from the perf files: the protected driver with restart 10 costs 0.367, 0.336, 0.255, 0.370 of the shipped restart 40 (fhn3d, cusp1d, burgers2d, bruss1d). B(restart 40)/A(restart 10) = 0.972, 1.111, 0.744, 1.407. B(10)/A(10) = 0.766, 0.760, 0.636, 0.776. I re-ran fhn3d A and B at restart 10 with the HEAD binary: all fields and state bits identical. Control arm B0 (client with shipped cadence) costs 0.945 to 0.967 of A, so the driver difference is about 5%. In the exploratory Krylov-budget-limited cell (bruss1d_stiff600, one tolerance) B/A is 0.771, above 0.67. The frozen row compares with A as shipped, so the verdict is unaffected.
findings.correction: Record that cadence PASS is relative to the shipped restart 40; that at equal restart length 10 the per-column test alone is worth 0.64 to 0.78 in instructions (exploratory, one tolerance); that a shorter restart in the protected driver's own configuration is an untested alternative lever; and that the result does not cover the budget-limited regime.

findings.claim: Timing protocol and re-measurement rule were followed.
findings.evidence: Confirmed for the quality rule: every try is kept (75 timing logs plus the interrupted cusp1d 1e-7 round 4 log), no cell has more than three measurements, the first try that meets load <= 8 and spread <= 10% is used (try 2 for 19 cells; burgers2d 1e-4 try 2 misses with a spread of 0.104 in arm C and try 3 is used), arm order rotates by round in every run, all timed runs end in the state hash of the instruction runs. Deviations from the letter of PREDECLARED timing.load_wait (wait bounded at 20 minutes): try 1 started at 15:12:31, minute 8 of the poll (15:04:16 to 15:24:17), and tries 2 and 3 were made six days later on a quiet host. Try 1 of cusp1d 1e-7 mixes rounds 0-3 from 2026-11-17 with rounds 4-8 from 2026-11-23; it misses on load either way. The cusp1d 1e-3 to 1e-5 invocations held the timing lock for 130 to 238 s each.
findings.correction: No change to verdicts. Record the two load_wait deviations.

findings.claim: cusp1d is decided at matched achieved error like the other families.
findings.evidence: The end-point error of cusp1d is erratic: at rtol 1e-4 arms A and B, which use the same threshold, end with E 1.81e-3 and 1.44e-4 (factor 12.6); A's error is not monotone (6.70e-7 at 1e-6, 9.47e-7 at 1e-7). My own reference (own right-hand side, DOP853 1e-12) agrees with the builder's to 1.9e-11, so this is a property of the runs, not of the reference. The verdicts on this family do not depend on the matching: the worst pairing across all tolerances gives instructions B_max/A_min 0.577, wall A_min/B_max 1.80, instructions C_max/A_min 0.236.
findings.correction: Report cusp1d as noise-limited for matched-error statements, with the worst-pairing bounds as the robust figures.
